target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections (Node.js terminates the process by default) or skip owned cleanup:

1. **Webhook shutdown `bot.stop()` rejection**: if `bot.stop()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), and owned cleanup—`closeTransportOnce()`, `status.noteWebhookStop()`, `stopDiagnosticHeartbeat()`—was silently skipped, leaking sockets and leaving stale status.
2. **Ingress worker stop not idempotent**: calling `stop()` twice created a second `stop` postMessage and a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/finally` so cleanup always runs even through rejection. The caller-side `.catch()` routes the error to `runtime.error` but the `finally` block guarantees transport close, status update, and diagnostics stop independent of the `bot.stop()` outcome.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a shared `stopPromise` for idempotency (same promise on repeated calls), catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes or socket leaks during Telegram channel restart or shutdown. Cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) always completes even if `bot.stop()` fails.

## Evidence

### Forward Proof — All Tests Pass

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
   Duration  22.76s
```

### Negative Control — Ingress Worker Stop Not Idempotent

```bash
# Revert ingress worker to origin/main (no stopPromise guard)
git checkout origin/main -- extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Result: ❌ **FAILED** — `stop()` returns distinct promises; `stop1 !== stop2`
```
AssertionError: expected Promise{…} to be Promise{…} // Object.is equality
 ❯ extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts:60:19
      expect(stop1).toBe(stop2);
```

Restore fix → ✅ **PASSED** (2/2).

### Negative Control — Webhook Shutdown Skips Cleanup When bot.stop() Throws

`bot.stop()` (line 1015) has no `try/finally` — if it rejects, `closeTransportOnce()`, `status.noteWebhookStop()`, and `stopDiagnosticHeartbeat()` are all skipped, leaking the owned undici transport and leaving stale status.

### Changes

- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`: wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/finally` so cleanup runs unconditionally
- `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts`: assert `transportCloseSpies[0]` called once through the finally block even when `bot.stop()` rejects
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`: idempotent `stop()` with shared stop promise, catch `postMessage` and `terminate` errors
- `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts`: tests for stop idempotency and terminate rejection handling

---
